subject: math

entries: Reading a pie chart: who likes what?: 6 of 12 pupils chose apples (1/2), and 3 each chose bananas and grapes (1/4 each).
slots.label: Reading a pie chart
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Reading a line graph: a rising trend: plants sold climb from Jan 20 to Apr 50 overall, with a small dip to 30 in March.
slots.label: Reading a line graph
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Worked example: comparing two bars of data: soccer has 13 votes and badminton has 8 votes, so 13 - 8 = 5 more chose soccer.
slots.label: Worked example
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Watch out: a steeper line is not always bigger: both shops rose from 20 to 40, a rise of +20 each, but graph B only looks flatter because its axis runs 0 to 200 instead of 0 to 50.
slots.label: Watch out
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A circle split into wedges that show fractions of a whole: in the animation the whole is 12 pupils, with apples 1/2, bananas 1/4 and grapes 1/4.
slots.label: Pie chart
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Points joined by a line to show how a value changes over time: plants sold were Jan 20, Feb 35, Mar 30 and Apr 50.
slots.label: Line graph
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Bars whose heights show amounts that can be compared: soccer 13 votes, badminton 8 votes and swimming 3 votes.
slots.label: Bar chart
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The numbers along an axis that say what the drawing stands for: graph A runs 0 to 50 while graph B runs 0 to 200.
slots.label: Axis scale
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: Data graphs: pie charts and line graphs
